=={{header|Cxc}}==

Cxc has no <code>while</code> loop; iteration folds into the atom lifecycle. The <code>main</code> atom carries a counter field <code>n</code>, enters <code>running</code>, and self-sends <code>tick</code>. Each tick reads <code>word_for</code>, prints it, advances <code>n</code> via the <code>=&gt;</code> transition arrow, and self-sends until the terminal guard <code>n &gt; 100</code> fires the arm whose target is <code>end</code>.

<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
def main:
    n: Int! = 1

    word_for :- String!
        ||: n % 15 == 0 : "FizzBuzz"
        ||: n % 3  == 0 : "Fizz"
        ||: n % 5  == 0 : "Buzz"
        ||: else        : n.to_string()

    -> running
        then: self :> tick

    running <: tick -> end
        |: n > 100

    running <: tick -> running
        then:
            print(self.word_for)
            n => n + 1
            self :> tick
</syntaxhighlight>

<code>word_for</code> is a zero-arg observation over the field <code>n</code>: a named, typed derivation with no lifecycle of its own. Inside it, <code>||: guard : body</code> is an expression-position multi-arm dispatch — the first arm whose guard holds yields its body value. It replaces <code>if</code> / <code>else if</code> / <code>else</code>; cxc has no <code>if</code> expression at v1.0.

The receive-side uses two <code>&lt;:</code> arms. First-match dispatch resolves them in source order: the terminal arm with the <code>|: n &gt; 100</code> guard fires before the unguarded self-looping arm can be reached. <code>:&gt;</code> is an asynchronous self-send that enqueues the next <code>tick</code> on the atom's own serial dispatch queue; the arm body runs to completion before the next tick's guards are evaluated.
